name: Oceanus Procellarum
description: The largest mare on the Moon, a vast basaltic plain covering much of the western near side.

name: Mare Imbrium
description: The 'Sea of Showers', a large lava-filled impact basin in the north-west of the near side.

name: Mare Serenitatis
description: The 'Sea of Serenity', a circular mare north-east of the near-side centre.

name: Mare Tranquillitatis
description: The 'Sea of Tranquillity', site of the first crewed landing (Apollo 11).

name: Mare Crisium
description: The 'Sea of Crises', an isolated, nearly circular mare near the eastern limb.

name: Mare Fecunditatis
description: The 'Sea of Fertility', east of Mare Tranquillitatis, sampled by Luna 16.

name: Mare Nubium
description: The 'Sea of Clouds', a mare in the south-west of the near side.

name: Mare Cognitum
description: The 'Known Sea', named after Ranger 7 returned the first close-up images of it.

name: Mare Insularum
description: The 'Sea of Islands', between Copernicus and Kepler; Surveyor 3 and Apollo 12 landed at its edge.

name: Mare Frigoris
description: The 'Sea of Cold', a long narrow mare stretching across the far north of the near side.

name: Sinus Medii
description: The 'Bay of the Centre', the small mare at the centre of the near side.

name: Lacus Excellentiae
description: The 'Lake of Excellence', a small mare in the south-west where SMART-1 impacted.

name: Copernicus
description: A young, bright crater with terraced walls and central peaks, surrounded by prominent rays.

name: Tycho
description: Young crater (about 100 million years old) in the southern highlands, source of the Moon's brightest ray system.

name: Kepler
description: Bright rayed crater in Oceanus Procellarum.

name: Autolycus
description: Crater in Mare Imbrium near which Luna 2 made the first impact on the Moon.

name: Alphonsus
description: Large old crater with a central peak and dark volcanic deposits on its floor; target of Ranger 9.

name: Fra Mauro
description: Old, heavily eroded crater; the hilly formation around it was the Apollo 14 landing site.

name: Le Monnier
description: Lava-flooded crater on the eastern edge of Mare Serenitatis, explored by the Lunokhod 2 rover.

name: Atlas
description: Crater in the north-east of the near side, target of the Hakuto-R Mission 1 landing attempt.

name: Furnerius
description: Old crater near the south-eastern limb; Hiten impacted nearby.

name: Gill
description: Crater in the south-eastern highlands near which Kaguya impacted.

name: Pontécoulant
description: Crater in the southern highlands; Luna 25 crashed nearby.

name: Goldschmidt
description: Large old crater near the north pole; the GRAIL twins impacted a mountain nearby.

name: Shioli
description: Very small crater near Theophilus, precision landing target of Japan's SLIM.

name: Malapert A
description: Small crater near the Malapert massif in the south polar region, where IM-1 Odysseus landed.

name: Sundman V
description: Small far-side crater; LADEE impacted its eastern rim.

name: Einstein
description: Large crater on the western limb; a SpaceX upper stage fell between it and Bell.

name: Bell
description: Far-side crater just beyond the western limb, north-west of Einstein.

name: Von Kármán
description: Lava-flooded crater inside the South Pole–Aitken basin, where Chang'e 4 made the first far-side landing.

name: Cabeus
description: Permanently shadowed south polar crater; the LCROSS impacts here confirmed water ice.

name: Shackleton
description: Crater almost exactly at the south pole: its rim gets near-constant sunlight and its floor is in permanent shadow.

name: Shoemaker
description: Permanently shadowed crater near the south pole, where Lunar Prospector was crashed to look for water.

name: Apollo basin
description: Large far-side impact basin within South Pole–Aitken; Chang'e 6 returned the first far-side samples from it.

name: Mons Rümker
description: Volcanic plateau of domes in Oceanus Procellarum; landing site of the Chang'e 5 sample-return mission.

name: Mons Latreille
description: Volcanic feature in Mare Crisium near which Firefly's Blue Ghost landed.

name: Mons Mouton
description: High plateau-like mountain near the south pole, landing site of IM-2 Athena.

name: Hadley–Apennine
description: Valley at the foot of the Montes Apenninus beside Hadley Rille; Apollo 15 landing site.

name: Taurus–Littrow
description: Valley on the edge of Mare Serenitatis; site of Apollo 17, the last crewed landing.

name: Descartes Highlands
description: Highland plateau explored by Apollo 16, the first crewed landing in the lunar highlands.

name: Apollonius highlands
description: Rugged highlands between Mare Crisium and Mare Fecunditatis, sampled by Luna 20.

name: Lunar south pole
description: Region of permanently shadowed craters that may hold water ice; main target of Artemis and other current missions.
